work_order.understanding:
Issue #66 carries two review findings left open by the review of PR #65, both re-measured on HEAD (7ee139f) before planning. (1) The beforeEach comment block in packages/loot-core/src/platform/server/sqlite/index.test.ts is badly rewrapped: measured widths for lines 23-31 are 78, 79, 79, 71, 78, 50, 79, 78, 6, so line 28 is a 50-character stub in a block otherwise wrapped at 71-79, and line 31 is a 6-character orphan. The clause spanning 26-28 reads 'but before the / beforeEach below re-armed it, from the second test on, global.fetch was the / real jsdom fetch again', where 'it' has no antecedent inside its own clause - the nearest singular noun is 'the global.fetch spy' two clauses back at line 24, so a reader can plausibly attach it to init() or to sql.js. That sentence is the one this comment exists to justify, so it is the one that has to be unambiguous. (2) The repo has a release-notes convention (packages/docs/docs/contributing/index.md:105, 'Add a release note', with no documented test-only exemption) and a validating gate at packages/ci-actions/bin/release-notes-check.mjs that refuses a diff adding no note under upcoming-release-notes/; PR #65 added none. I decided to satisfy the convention rather than exempt the change, on the evidence that this fork's own sibling follow-up PR #60 shipped upcoming-release-notes/fix-command-bar-dialog-console-drain.md for a purely e2e-test change. Nothing here is user-visible, nothing runs in the browser, and no product behaviour changes.

v1 was rejected for prescribing a 'so' on line 27 that asserts the reverse of the truth, and for rejecting the reviewer's 70-char wording on a 71-column floor that nothing in this repo enforces. Both are corrected below.
work_order.root_cause: The work order that produced PR #65 prescribed the replacement comment as pre-wrapped literal text; inserting it changed the paragraph's line breaks without reflowing, so 're-armed it' landed as 're-armed it, from the second test on, global.fetch was the' / 'real jsdom fetch again. patchFetchForSqlJS is a'. The pronoun was in the prescribed wording too, so this is a suggestion on the order as much as on the code - this plan reflows the paragraph and names the referent. The missing release note is the same shape: the convention at packages/docs/docs/contributing/index.md:105 has no test-only exemption, and PR #65 shipped a test-only diff without one.

1. Reflow lines 27-28 of the beforeEach comment in packages/loot-core/src/platform/server/sqlite/index.test.ts. Replace exactly those two lines; lines 23-26 and 29-31 stay byte-identical. The paragraph as a whole becomes the nine lines below, at the widths measured here:

  78  // The afterEach below calls vi.restoreAllMocks(), which is file-scoped rather
  79  // than spy-scoped, so it takes down the global.fetch spy this file's beforeAll
  79  // installed along with the console spies. Nothing breaks today, because init()
  71  // has already run and sql.js caches the compiled wasm — but before the
  70  // beforeEach below re-armed the fetch patch, from the second test on,
  71  // global.fetch was the real jsdom fetch again. patchFetchForSqlJS is a
  79  // vi.spyOn(...).mockImplementation(...) with no restore of its own, so calling
  78  // it once per test is idempotent and the blanket restore can no longer outrun
   6  // it.

One wording change, in service of the complaint: 're-armed it' becomes 're-armed the fetch patch', so the referent is named rather than left for the reader to infer. This is the reviewer's own suggested sentence from issue #66, transcribed without alteration. Its line lands at 70 columns - one under the 71 that lines 23-29 mostly occupy, and that is deliberate and correct: the width is a wrapping artefact, not a rule. Nothing in this repo enforces a minimum comment width (.oxlintrc.json defines no max-len or min-len rule, and oxfmt is configured with printWidth 80 but does not reflow comment prose), so a 70-column line that reads better is not a defect. Do not add a connective to reach 71. Specifically, do NOT insert 'so' after the comma on line 27: 'so' marks a consequence, and the consequence of the beforeEach re-arming the fetch patch is that global.fetch STAYS mocked - whereas the sentence describes the state in which that re-arm had not yet happened. As written with 'so' it asserts that the re-arm is what made fetch real again, which is the reverse of the truth, and it is the one sentence this ticket exists to make unambiguous. 70 is also the length the reviewer proposed, and a 1-column shortfall is not a reason to prefer a sentence that says the wrong thing.

Do not touch line 31's 6-character orphan - the reviewer asked for the paragraph to end as it does today, and it is a sentence-ending line, not the mid-paragraph stub the finding was about. Do not reflow lines 23-26 either: line 26's 71 columns is the block's existing floor and is not part of the finding.

Evidence: beforeAll at index.test.ts:17-21 is `beforeAll(async () => { patchFetchForSqlJS(baseURL); return init({ baseURL }); });` and contains zero occurrences of the string 'console' (`sed -n '17,21p' | grep -c console` -> 0). All four console spies are created inside test bodies: `grep -n 'vi.spyOn(console'` on the PR branch file returns only lines 81, 160, 311, 379, each assigned to a `const consoleSpy` local. packages/loot-core/src/mocks/util.ts:67-82 shows patchFetchForSqlJS touches only `global.fetch`. The file's own describe-level comment at index.test.ts:46-51 already states the correct fact ('Five of the ten tests mock console.log ... The other five mock no console.log'), which contradicts line 25's attachment.

The work order explicitly routed this call to the review stage, so naming it is the point of this finding.

review.title: The PR title is missing the mandatory `[AI]` prefix. `.github/agents/pr-and-commit-rules.md` states 'ALL pull request titles MUST be prefixed with [AI]' and gives 'Fix type error in account validation' (MISSING PREFIX — NOT ALLOWED) as the counterexample.
